summary: Shun'ei Hirai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1956–1974) and Komazawa University. He held multiple posts at Komazawa University, serving as lecturer (1964), professor (1970, 1976, 1990), and vice president (1986).
Shunei Mori is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a part-time lecturer at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 1995).
Shunei Tsuboi was a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Bukkyo University, with his tenure attested in 1963 and 1972.

Shunji Hosaka specializes in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Waseda University (~1975–1980), he taught at Reitaku University (~1988–1996) and Chuo University (~1996), and held posts attested in 2026 at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Shunkyo Katsumata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He held a post at Toyo University and served at Taisho University (~1946–1983), where he became professor emeritus.

Shunryu Suzuki was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and Eihei-ji, and under teachers including Gyokujun So-on. He served as abbot at Zoun-in, Rinsouin, and Sokoji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center.

Shunsho Manabe worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, having studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1963). He held a post at Hosen Gakuen College and served as a professor at Shikoku University (~1998–2012).
Shunsho Terakawa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held an appointment at Otani University (~1965–2000), becoming professor emeritus.
Shuntaro Kondo is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD from Ryukoku University by 2011. He was attested as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University in 2012.

Shuntaro Matsuyama specialized in Indology and religious studies, studying at the University of Tokyo and under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1949–1953). He taught at Bigakko, Kokugakuin University, Tama Art University, and as a professor at Joshibi University of Art and Design.

Shunzo Onoda is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a D.Lit. at Bukkyo University by 1993. He served at Bukkyo University as an associate professor (attested 1996) and professor (attested 2005).

Shuyu Kanaoka specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1952) and earning a doctorate from Toyo University (1962). He served as an assistant professor at Toyo University (~1968–1992).
Shuyu Sakurai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University until 1943. He was attested as professor emeritus at Komazawa University between 1982 and 1992.
Shwe Zan Aung was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a B.A. from the University of Rangoon in 1891. In 1895, he studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw.
Shōkō Kabutogi was a Buddhist studies scholar who graduated from Rissho University in 1936. He later served as a professor at Rissho University, attested in 1972.

Shōren Ihara was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as an assistant professor at Kyushu University (attested 1959–1965, 1977) and was a member of the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998).

Shōshin Ichishima is a Buddhist studies scholar who was a visiting lecturer at the University of Hawaiʻi. At Taisho University, he served as Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and was attested as professor emeritus in 2014.

Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under J. Sitaramamma (attested 2014). They also studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Sayadaw U Kundala and Sayadaw U Ghosita.

Sibani Das Gupta was an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka and earned a doctorate from the University of Calcutta in 1954. Her mentors included teacher Rajendra Chandra Hazra and doctoral supervisor Sushil Kumar De.

Sibaraj Chetry is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma and teachers including D. K. Chakravarty. He served as a lecturer of philosophy at North Lakhimpur College (attested 2012).
